Farol Research

A working prototype for equity research and portfolio management on Brazilian banks. All figures are computed from the local IF.Data pipeline; no live market data is shown.

Source

Banco Central do Brasil, IF.Data — prudential conglomerates, Type 1. Reported figures from IFRS filings. Panel: 13 quarters ending 2026 Q2.

Use

Research and illustration only. Not investment advice. Conglomerate figures are not directly comparable with the listed holding company.

Methodology

How to read this page

The panel tracks 34 institutions in IF.Data: the five large universal banks, the federal and regional public banks, the listed mid-caps and the payments and fintech lenders.

Definitions

ROE (TTM)
Net income over the last four quarters ÷ average shareholders' equity over the same period.
ROA (TTM)
Net income TTM ÷ average total assets.
Intermediation margin (TTM)
Net interest income plus payment-transaction revenue, TTM ÷ average total assets.
Cost of risk
Credit provisions TTM ÷ total credit portfolio. Higher is worse.
Coverage
Expected credit loss allowance ÷ gross credit. Higher is more conservative.
Efficiency ratio
Personnel and administrative expenses ÷ (net interest income + fees + services + payment revenue). Higher is worse.
NPL (system)
Loans at least 15 days overdue ÷ the credit portfolio. Published at panel level, not per institution.

Aggregation

Stock items are sums. ROE is aggregate net income over aggregate equity; cost of risk and coverage are weighted by credit; efficiency is the median institution, to avoid one outlier dominating a small sample. Shares are of panel assets at the selected quarter.

Known breaks

The BCB changed the total-panel NPL definition to problem assets (ratings E–H) in 2025 Q1. This page charts household and corporate NPL at ≥15 days, which remain continuous; the total series is excluded. The 2024 Q4 credit report is missing from the source, so the risk series breaks there rather than interpolating.

Scope

IF.Data reports the prudential conglomerate. That is wider than the individual bank and narrower than the listed holding: insurance, for example, sits in the holding and explains most of the bridge in section 05.
